stories.summary: AI researcher Yoshua Bengio says mounting safety concerns could push governments toward a Covid-style moment of decisive regulation. The Guardian reports that he pointed to recent events involving OpenAI agents as evidence that a safety crisis may spur action to protect the public.

links.headline: ‘Godfather of AI’ says tech regulation is nearing Covid-style pivot moment
links.excerpt: Safety crisis makes it more likely that governments will be spurred into action, says Yoshua Bengio Concerns over AI safety are reaching a point where governments realise they must act to protect the public, similarly to in the Covid pandemic, according to one of the “godfathers” of the technology.
